items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Freeman opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which many of us are gathered today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishnaabe and Neutral peoples. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous people with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Freeman provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: 2024 Sustainability and Climate Change
notes: Ena Ristic gave a presentation with the strategic, corporate and community sustainability highlights, as well as an overview of engagement and the challenges they face. She then responded to questions. Bob Henderson, Mark Dykstra and Sandy Little also responded to questions of Council.

Kae Elgie, Resident of Waterloo, GreenWR spoke about the positive impact the City is making, and how the members of the public can keep track of the community’s progress. She then responded to questions of Council. Ena Ristic and Sandy Little also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Public Meetings
notes: The Formal Public meeting for Official Plan Amendment No. 52 & Zoning By-law Amendment Application Z-24-03, 14688210 Canada Inc, 177-179 Albert Street, Ward 7 Uptown, which was scheduled to occur on Monday, April 22nd, has been deferred to a later date to be determined.
For more information regarding the application please contact the planner Max Kerrigan at max.kerrigan@waterloo.ca or 519-747-8522.

items.title: Official Plan Amendment No. 48 and
notes: John Vos gave a presentation outlining the proposed development and amendments required. He then responded to questions of Council.

Trevor Hawkins, Partner, MHBC Planning gave a presentation further detailing the proposed development and the context of the site. He then responded to questions of Council. Tommy Rakic, Owner, Copper Bay Homes also responded to questions of Council.

Robert Barnett, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the proposed amendments, affordable housing, the recommendations as presented in the report, and the need for a Master Plan for the lands between Dietz and Avondale.
Thom Bartleman, Resident of Waterloo spoke against the proposed development, citing the reduction of parking and suitability for the neighbourhood. He then responded to questions of Council.
Ashwin Annamalai, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the troubles of renting in the City and the need for more housing, especially purpose-built rentals.
Phil Marfisi, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the need for transit-oriented development and that they supported a mid-rise building planned for a side street.
Reinhold Dresler, Resident of Waterloo spoke about concerns with the height of the building.
Shiva Subramanian, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the need for more rental housing. They then responded to questions of Council.
Craig Sloss, Resident of Waterloo spoke in favour of the proposed development, about the breakdown of the building, and about the importance of protecting the countryside.
Pauline Campbell, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the suitability of the building to the neighbourhood, as well as the impact of the building on Waterloo Heights.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application was open to Council for a motion and debate.
Joel Cotter and John Vos responded to questions of Council.

items.title: General Amendments to the Official Plan
notes: The Corporation of the City of Waterloo
Tristin Deveau gave a presentation outlining the proposed amendments to the Official Plan and Zoning By-law.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application is now open to Council for a motion and debate.
Councillor Vasic having previously declared a pecuniary interest was absent for the taking of the vote.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Hanmer noted that she was proud and excited about residents not just in her ward but across the City being engaged in Earth Day activities over the past weekend.
There was a lot of cleanup across the City. She offered her thanks to those who organized the events as well as those who participated.

Councillor Bodaly appeared as acting mayor when the solicitor general was in town last week. They visited Fire Station 2 in his ward to discuss cancer screening information for firefighters in the community.

Councillor Roe mentioned that the Coalition of Muslim Women held an Eid activity event at the Harper Library on Saturday, April 20. The crafts were great and there was great engagement with the community.

motions.text: 1. That Council approve report COM2024-010. 2. That Council approve the revisions to the Corporate Policy A-033 Green Building Policy for City-Owned Buildings as Appendix A. 3. That Council direct staff to update greenhouse gas emission targets for City-owned buildings to align with Council’s most recently endorsed greenhouse gas emission reduction targets of 50% by 2030 and net-zero by 2050. 4.
